profile.campus: Sandston, Henrico County, Virginia (QTS Richmond 1 campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, this Sandston, Virginia campus, Richmond 1 (RIC1), spans 207 acres, totals 2.3 million sq ft of current space, and provides 238 MW of campus power capacity across six DC buildings (DC1-DC6), described by QTS as the largest and most connected data center campus in the area; DC1-DC3 share the address 6000 Technology Blvd, Sandston, VA 23150. This is a campus-aggregate figure across multiple buildings, not confirmed as any single building's individual capacity.

QTS Data Centers (the operator name shown on this row, "Quality Technology Services," is the company's pre-2013-IPO name; it now formally operates as QTS Realty Trust and trades under the domain q.com after qtsdatacenters.com was retired) was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor at the center of the company's operations alongside its operations-support center in Suwanee, Georgia.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
The Richmond 1 campus near Richmond, Virginia encompasses 207 acres, 2.3 million square feet of built space, and 238 MW of power capacity across at least six buildings at multiple addresses in Henrico County and Sandston. This aggregate figure ranks it among Virginia's largest published data center campuses, though not in the top 23 by operator disclosure; 23 facilities in Virginia publish capacity figures totaling 1375 MW, and this campus represents 17 percent of that published total. The campus was built on a former semiconductor manufacturing site starting in 2010, and the operator describes it as the largest and most connected data center campus in the region.

At typical AI training power density of 40 kW per rack, the campus's 238 MW would support roughly 6000 racks. Current tenant composition is not published. The campus certifications and specific tenant suitability are not disclosed on the operator's published specification page. Whether this campus hosts GPU clusters, CPU systems, or conventional IT load cannot be determined from the operator's public materials.

The state context for this campus is incomplete. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities but only 23 with published power figures, so this campus is visible only because its operator publishes capacity. The grid constraints on Virginia's available power for further AI data center growth are not published here. The campus's power supply source, renewable energy fraction, and available headroom for expansion are not disclosed.
